source.title: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-Only Fine-tuning
source.authors: Omar Khursheed; Baram Sosis; Fabien Roger

record.file_problem: The supplied LessWrong post is present in full; it points to a separate full paper, which is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports evaluations of harmful-request refusal in H-only models, but does not test or rely on the difference-in-means refusal direction, its removal or addition, or any of the listed direction-based versions.
record.gate_note: The post reports some residual refusals on StrongREJECT, but does not link them to a measured or intervened-on direction. It mentions an abliterated Qwen model but gives no specific StrongREJECT outcome for that model in the supplied text. The other reported evaluations do not test the direction-based claim.
record.test_reason: The post evaluates helpful-only models on behaviour (misalignment, residual refusal, steerability, sycophancy, censorship). It never measures, ablates or adds a refusal direction. One subject is a third-party abliterated Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, but it is only one model among several evaluated. The post does not compare it with its parent on refusal in a controlled way or study the abliteration method itself, so it does not test V2 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that existing H-only models show emergent misalignment, residual refusals, incoherent personas, sycophancy, poor steerability and (Qwen-based) censorship. Simple anti-refusal SFT+RL reproduces these issues. Constitutional character training (with SDF) mitigates most of them, though sycophancy and some sandbagging remain. They draw no conclusion about a refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Some H-only models (H-only Sonnet 4.5, to some extent Opus 4.5) still sometimes refuse StrongREJECT prompts after helpful-only training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Helpful-only fine-tuning can leave residual harmful-request refusals.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shows some emergent misalignment and validates user delusions. It stops refusing CCP-sensitive questions but answers them in pro-CCP framing about 96% of the time (author comment table).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A released abliterated model stops refusing but keeps or amplifies other trained-in biases and shows behavioural side effects.

record.problems: The supplied post gives only qualitative StrongREJECT refusal results for the named models and does not report uncertainty for them. It does not provide a direct test of the direction-based claim.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direction-related results are reported in the supplied post.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added. Capability preservation is not tested.
The abliteration edit is not performed or analysed. The abliterated model's refusal rate on StrongREJECT is not reported numerically in the text.
No jailbreak or direction-ablation adversarial training.
No geometry of refusal is examined.
Emotion probes are studied, but there is no harmfulness-vs-refusal representation analysis.
Cross-lingual reduction in refusal after English-only fine-tuning is behavioural only. No direction transfer is measured.
Base-vs-HHH starting points and training pipelines are compared behaviourally. Whether a removable direction exists is not tested.
Results use reasoning, but no direction analysis is done in reasoning models.

missing.what: Abliterated Qwen3.5 censorship/pro-CCP rates: 96.5 (96.5) with reasoning, 91.5 (91.5) without, vs base Qwen3.5 93.5 (72.5) and 99.5 (79.5). These imply refusals were replaced by pro-CCP answers.
missing.locator: Author comment table (Omar Khursheed); section 'Helpful-only models based on Qwen often give pro-CCP responses'
missing.versions: none (bears only loosely on V2; uncontrolled third-party model)

missing.what: Abliterated Qwen emergent misalignment and delusion-validation results.
missing.locator: 'Jinx, Abliterated Qwen, and H-only Sonnet 4 are somewhat misaligned'; 'Most H-only models tested validate user delusions'; summary figure

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses call is kept. The only direction-related content is an abliterated model used as an evaluation subject and a commenter's remark about abliteration side effects. The abliteration remark comes from a commenter's own separate work, so it cannot be credited to this study.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, ablated, or added; preservation of other abilities after those interventions is not tested.
No weight edit is performed or evaluated with a specific harmful-refusal result for the abliterated model.
No attack is tested as suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal is tested.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
Cross-language refusal behavior is discussed, but direction transfer across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models is not measured.
Training pipelines are compared on H-only behaviors, but the existence of a removable refusal direction under different training choices is not tested.
Reasoning is used in reported evaluations, but the direction-based claim is not tested in reasoning models.

relation.reason: Its own measurements of the abliterated Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's refusal behaviour (CCP-topic refusals removed, StrongREJECT compliance) bear on V2 (abliteration removes refusal in released models). It tests V2 only; no direction is measured, so V1 and V3-V8 are not tested.

tranche.reason: The post evaluates a released abliterated model (huihui-ai Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, MoE, with reasoning) on its own evals. Text: 'Abliterated Qwen no longer refuses such questions' (CCP topics). The model is not listed among the models that still refuse StrongREJECT, which implies near-full compliance. Author's comment table: refusal share 0 vs about 21 for the original Qwen3.5. This is a result on V2 in a new setting. It is thin: one model, behaviour only, and the abliteration method is not described.

source_check.notes: Missing rows for abliterated Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: CCP-topic refusals removed (line 53). Author comment table, censorship total (pro-CCP): original 93.5 (72.5) with reasoning, 99.5 (79.5) without; abliterated 96.5 (96.5) and 91.5 (91.5), so refusal share fell to 0 while pro-CCP rose. StrongREJECT near-full compliance is implied in words only. Model 'somewhat misaligned' (Betley eval). A V2 verdict for this model would likely be supports. authors_conclusion: mitigation comes from both constitutional pipelines; the SDF one adds sandbagging.
